text:
Philadelphia arrives in Calgary on game two of a five-game road trip, 0-1-0 so far, after a 3-2 loss at the Rangers. The Flyers are 1-3-1 in their last five and are without Rasmus Ristolainen. The Flames are 2-2-1 over the same stretch and came off a 5-3 home loss to Anaheim, blowing a two-goal lead on a goal with 1:34 left. Calgary is also missing Kevin Bahl, Connor Zary and Samuel Honzek. The Flames are better than their record: their goal difference is -18 against about -9 on chance quality, partly from finishing and goaltending running cold.

Our numbers see a tight game, with Calgary at 2.91 expected goals to Philadelphia's 2.76. At five on five, CGY has 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against 41% for PHI. Calgary's power play is the weaker unit, 0.39 expected goals a game to 0.66 for the Flyers, and the Flames take 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps handing out chances. In net, projected starters Dan Vladar (PHI) and Devin Cooley (CGY) are separated this season: Cooley is at +2.19 goals saved above expected, Vladar at -0.21. Last season they were closer, +17.23 over 31 games for Cooley and +12.74 over 52 for Vladar.

For the Flyers, Matvei Michkov has 11 points in his last ten and the extra chances back it up, with a 26% chance to score and 52% to record a point. Trevor Zegras (27% to score) leads our list. For Calgary, Joel Farabee, a former Flyers first-rounder, scored on the power play Friday and sits at 30% to score. Matvei Gridin, 20% to score, has eight points in ten games, though we see that as mostly bounces.
